newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israel withdraws threat to sue British Airways.
newsitem.headline: Israel withdraws threat to sue British Airways.

text.p: Israel's Civil Aviation Authority withdrew its threat to sue British Airways over the airline's new sales promotion because the two sides have agreed jointly to examine the issue, the Transport Ministry said on Tuesday.
If the two sides cannot settle the dispute within 10 days the issue will be sent to an unspecified third party for settlement, the ministry said in a statement.
The British carrier in the meantime will continue its campaign, which allows passengers flying from Tel Aviv to non-European destinations via London to purchase a companion ticket at half fare.
The Civil Aviation Authority contended that the promotion infringed the aviation agreement signed by the two countries.
The decision to hold discussions between the legal advisers of both sides was taken at the initiative of the Transport Ministry's director general Nahum Langental.
British Airways claims that the promotion, initiated by its general manager in Tel Aviv, Nira Dor, is in accordance with Israeli regulations.
A British Airways spokesman declined to give details on the number of promotional tickets booked in the first week but travel industry sources said it was in the hundreds.
British Airways said the latest fare war was started by El Al Israel Airlines, which is offering roundtrip tickets to London during the winter season for $333 and to New York for $899.
The Civil Aviation Authority had said British Airway's promotion would hurt not only El Al, Israel's state-owned carrier, but U.S. airlines that fly to Israel, such as TWA.

The authority's director general Menachem Sharon has said that fares between Israel and the United States are already highly competitive and noted that in the past two years two U.S. airlines -- Delta Airlines and World Airways -- have halted their flights to Tel Aviv because of a lack of profits.
"We attribute great importance to British Airways continuing to operate in Israel alongside El Al and other carriers, albeit in compliance with international aviation agreements," Langental said.
